nodes.label: Forbidden state
nodes.sublabel: a screen state, not a crash

cards.title: The trust boundary
items: the client is untrusted: game state, prices, payments and entitlements are server-authoritative, and authorization stays on the server — hiding a screen or a button is UX, not access control
auth uses the system browser (OIDC + PKCE) or the identity slice; the app never holds the password and the system browser is the only place it is typed
the deep link and the push payload are untrusted input: parse them against the route allowlist, validate every parameter, and never perform a state-changing action from a link

cards.title: Tokens live in the OS keystore
items: TokenStore and SecretStore are ports; the keystore adapter is the only implementation — a token in AsyncStorage, MMKV, a log or the bundle is a finding
the SDK attaches the header; the View never reads the token and never imports the SDK — the View renders state and calls commands
clear user data on sign-out and tenant switch: a shared device is the default assumption

cards.title: Rotation and reuse detection
items: refresh rotation with reuse detection: a reused refresh token is a signal, and the family is revoked rather than silently re-issued
the push token has its own lifecycle — register on login, refresh on change, revoke on logout — and the server dedupes tokens per user and device
a 403 is a stable forbidden state the screen renders; jailbreak or root is a server-side risk signal, never a client-side block
